chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who divorced his wife three times, so she became independent from him, and he wanted to remarry her, so he said to her:

'I intend to remarry you, so marry another husband.' She said to him, 'I have married another husband and I have made myself lawful to you.' He asked: 'Will her word be believed and will he remarry her, and what should he do?' He said, 'If the woman is trustworthy, her word is believed.' And the second aspect in the narrations we presented earlier is that they can be attributed to a type of taqiyyah (dissimulation), because it is the school of Umar, so it is permissible that the situation necessitated that he (peace be upon him) gave a ruling in accordance with his school, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman says she married another man to allow her ex-husband to remarry her after three divorces?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *tawqi* (accepting the testimony) of a trustworthy woman in the context of *tahlil* (the 'fixer' marriage), allowing a man to remarry his thrice-divorced wife upon her declaration of a valid intermediate marriage. The text further contextualizes this ruling within the jurisprudential debate between the Ahl al-Bayt and the school of Umar, suggesting the Imam’s verdict may have been delivered via *taqiyyah* to align with the prevailing Sunni practice of the time, thereby highlighting the dynamic nature of Shia legal reasoning.
